# OpenACP **Self-hosted bridge between messaging platforms and AI coding agents** One message, any channel, any agent. [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE) [![Node.js >= 20](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-%3E%3D%2020-green.svg)](https://nodejs.org/) [![ACP Protocol](https://img.shields.io/badge/Protocol-ACP-purple.svg)](https://agentclientprotocol.org/) [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@openacp/cli.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@openacp/cli) [![Twitter Follow](https://img.shields.io/twitter/follow/Open_ACP?style=social)](https://x.com/Open_ACP) [Getting Started](docs/guide/getting-started.md) | [Agents](docs/guide/agents.md) | [Usage](docs/guide/usage.md) | [Configuration](docs/guide/configuration.md) | [Tunnel](docs/guide/tunnel.md) | [Plugins](docs/guide/plugins.md) | [Development](docs/guide/development.md)
--- ## What is OpenACP? OpenACP lets you control AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, ...) from messaging apps like Telegram. You send a message, the agent writes code, runs commands, and streams everything back — in real time. It uses the [Agent Client Protocol (ACP)](https://agentclientprotocol.org/) to talk to agents. You host it on your own machine, so you own the data. ``` You (Telegram / Discord / ...) ↓ OpenACP ─── ChannelAdapter ─── Session Manager ─── Session Store ↓ ↓ ACP Protocol (JSON-RPC / stdio) Tunnel Service ↓ ↓ AI Agent (Claude Code, Codex, ...) File/Diff Viewer ``` ## Screenshots <<<<<<< HEAD - [**Multi-agent**](docs/guide/configuration.md#agents) — Claude Code, Codex, or any ACP-compatible agent - [**Telegram**](docs/guide/telegram-setup.md) — Forum topics, real-time streaming, permission buttons, skill commands - [**Tunnel & Viewer**](docs/guide/tunnel.md) — Public file/diff viewer via Cloudflare, ngrok, bore, Tailscale - [**Session persistence**](docs/guide/usage.md#session-persistence--resume) — Lazy resume across restarts - [**Daemon mode**](docs/guide/usage.md#daemon-mode) — Background service with auto-start on boot - [**CLI runtime**](docs/guide/usage.md#cli-runtime-commands) — Create and manage sessions from the terminal - [**Config editor**](docs/guide/usage.md#config-editor) — Interactive `openacp config` for all settings - [**Setup wizard**](docs/guide/getting-started.md) — Interactive first-run setup with bot validation and auto-detect - [**Plugin system**](docs/guide/plugins.md) — Install channel adapters as npm packages - [**Structured logging**](docs/guide/configuration.md#logging) — Pino with rotation, per-session log files =======

## Supported Agents OpenACP follows the [Agent Client Protocol (ACP)](https://agentclientprotocol.com/) standard — an open protocol for connecting AI coding agents to client applications. Agent definitions are loaded from the [official ACP Registry](https://agentclientprotocol.com/get-started/registry) via CDN ([`registry.json`](https://cdn.agentclientprotocol.com/registry/v1/latest/registry.json)), so new agents are available as soon as they're registered. | Agent | Distribution | Description | |-------|-------------|-------------| | [Claude Agent](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code) | npx | Anthropic's Claude coding agent | | [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) | npx | Google's official CLI for Gemini | | [Codex CLI](https://github.com/openai/codex) | npx | OpenAI's coding assistant | | [GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli) | npx | GitHub's AI pair programmer | | [Cursor](https://www.cursor.com/) | binary | Cursor's coding agent | | [Cline](https://github.com/cline/cline) | npx | Autonomous coding agent with file editing, commands, and browser | | [goose](https://github.com/block/goose) | binary | Open source AI agent for engineering tasks | | [Amp](https://github.com/tao12345666333/amp-acp) | binary | The frontier coding agent | | [Auggie CLI](https://www.augmentcode.com/) | npx | Augment Code's agent with industry-leading context engine | | [Junie](https://www.jetbrains.com/) | binary | AI coding agent by JetBrains | | [Kilo](https://github.com/kilocode/kilo) | npx | The open source coding agent | | [Qwen Code](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code) | npx | Alibaba's Qwen coding assistant | | [crow-cli](https://github.com/crowdecode/crow-cli) | uvx | Minimal ACP native coding agent | | ...and more | | [See full registry →](https://agentclientprotocol.com/get-started/registry) | > **28+ agents supported** — any agent registered in the ACP Registry works out of the box. Install with `openacp agents install ` or browse from Telegram with `/agents`. ## Features - **Multi-agent** — Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and [28+ ACP-compatible agents](#supported-agents) - **Telegram** — Forum topics, real-time streaming, permission buttons, skill commands - **Tunnel & file viewer** — Public file/diff viewer via Cloudflare, ngrok, bore, or Tailscale - **Session persistence** — Resume sessions across restarts - --- ## What is OpenACP? OpenACP lets you control AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, ...) from messaging apps like Telegram. You send a message, the agent writes code, runs commands, and streams everything back — in real time. It uses the [Agent Client Protocol (ACP)](https://agentclientprotocol.org/) to talk to agents. You host it on your own machine, so you own the data. ``` You (Telegram / Discord / ...) ↓ OpenACP ─── ChannelAdapter ─── Session Manager ─── Session Store ↓ ↓ ACP Protocol (JSON-RPC / stdio) Tunnel Service ↓ ↓ AI Agent (Claude Code, Codex, ...) File/Diff Viewer ``` ## Screenshots

Manage sessions, agents, and settings
Agent at Work
Plans, reads files, writes code

Real-time Tool Calls
See every action the agent takes
Agent Skills
Brainstorming, TDD, debugging & more
## Supported Agents OpenACP follows the [Agent Client Protocol (ACP)](https://agentclientprotocol.com/) standard — an open protocol for connecting AI coding agents to client applications. Agent definitions are loaded from the [official ACP Registry](https://agentclientprotocol.com/get-started/registry) via CDN ([`registry.json`](https://cdn.agentclientprotocol.com/registry/v1/latest/registry.json)), so new agents are available as soon as they're registered. | Agent | Distribution | Description | |-------|-------------|-------------| | [Claude Agent](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code) | npx | Anthropic's Claude coding agent | | [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) | npx | Google's official CLI for Gemini | | [Codex CLI](https://github.com/openai/codex) | npx | OpenAI's coding assistant | | [GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli) | npx | GitHub's AI pair programmer | | [Cursor](https://www.cursor.com/) | binary | Cursor's coding agent | | [Cline](https://github.com/cline/cline) | npx | Autonomous coding agent with file editing, commands, and browser | | [goose](https://github.com/block/goose) | binary | Open source AI agent for engineering tasks | | [Amp](https://github.com/tao12345666333/amp-acp) | binary | The frontier coding agent | | [Auggie CLI](https://www.augmentcode.com/) | npx | Augment Code's agent with industry-leading context engine | | [Junie](https://www.jetbrains.com/) | binary | AI coding agent by JetBrains | | [Kilo](https://github.com/kilocode/kilo) | npx | The open source coding agent | | [Qwen Code](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code) | npx | Alibaba's Qwen coding assistant | | [crow-cli](https://github.com/crowdecode/crow-cli) | uvx | Minimal ACP native coding agent | | ...and more | | [See full registry →](https://agentclientprotocol.com/get-started/registry) | > **28+ agents supported** — any agent registered in the ACP Registry works out of the box. # Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs

Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.

Start by understanding the current project context, then ask questions one at a time to refine the idea. Once you understand what you're building, present the design and get user approval.

<HARD-GATE>
Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any project, or take any implementation action until you have presented a design and the user has approved it. This applies to EVERY project regardless of perceived simplicity.
</HARD-GATE>

## Anti-Pattern: "This Is Too Simple To Need A Design"

Every project goes through this process. A todo list, a single-function utility, a config change — all of them. "Simple" projects are where unexamined assumptions cause the most wasted work. The design can be short (a few sentences for truly simple projects), but you MUST present it and get approval.

## Checklist

You MUST create a task for each of these items and complete them in order:

1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Offer visual companion** (if topic will involve visual questions) — this is its own message, not combined with a clarifying question. See the Visual Companion section below.
3. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, understand purpose/constraints/success criteria
4. **Propose 2-3 approaches** — with trade-offs and your recommendation
5. **Present design** — in sections scaled to their complexity, get user approval after each section
6. **Write design doc** — save to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit
7. **Spec review loop** — dispatch spec-document-reviewer subagent with precisely crafted review context (never your session history); fix issues and re-dispatch until approved (max 3 iterations, then surface to human)
8. **User reviews written spec** — ask user to review the spec file before proceeding
9. **Transition to implementation** — invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan

## Process Flow

```dot

    "Explore project context" [shape=box];
    "Visual questions ahead?" [shape=diamond];
    "Offer Visual Companion\n(own message, no other content)" [shape=box];
    "Ask clarifying questions" [shape=box];
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" [shape=box];
    "Present design sections" [shape=box];
    "User approves design?" [shape=diamond];
    "Write design doc" [shape=box];
    "Spec review loop" [shape=box];
    "Spec review passed?" [shape=diamond];
```

## Code Review Issues from PR #19

Tracking issues identified during review of #19 ("Feat: Update cli for full handling function").

---

### Critical

- [ ] **Security: API server has no authentication** (`api-server.ts`) — Any local process can create/cancel sessions. Need file-based shared secret with restricted permissions.
- [ ] **Security: XML/systemd injection in `autostart.ts`** — `nodePath` and `cliPath` interpolated directly into plist XML and systemd unit files without escaping.
- [ ] **`getCurrentVersion()` uses `require()` in ESM module** (`cli.ts`) — Will throw `ReferenceError: require is not defined` at runtime. Should use `await import()`.
- [ ] **Race condition: `stopDaemon` removes PID file immediately after SIGTERM** (`daemon.ts`) — Should wait for process to actually exit.

### Major

- [ ] **`readBody` has no size limit** (`api-server.ts`) — Can exhaust memory. Enforce max body size.
- [ ] **API picks first adapter arbitrarily** (`api-server.ts`) — Unpredictable behavior with multiple adapters.
- [ ] **`reset` command doesn't check foreground mode** (`cli.ts`) — Can delete `~/.openacp` under a running foreground server.
- [ ] **Update check runs on every start** (`cli.ts`) — Blocks startup with network request, including daemon/boot. Should skip for `--daemon-child` and rate-limit.
- [ ] **`session.status` not set to error state on warmup failure** (`session.ts`)
- [ ] **API server auto-approves permissions for headless sessions** (`api-server.ts`) — Any local process can make agent execute without user confirmation.

### Minor

- [ ] Inconsistent quote style — new code uses single quotes, codebase uses double quotes
- [ ] `autostart.ts` reimplements `expandHome()` inline instead of using the imported function
- [ ] `logs` command uses `tail -f` — not portable
- [ ] `compareVersions` doesn't handle pre-release versions
- [ ] API server doesn't `decodeURIComponent` session ID in DELETE route

### Tests

- [ ] `startDaemon` and `stopDaemon` have zero test coverage
- [ ] `installAutoStart` and `uninstallAutoStart` have zero test coverage
- [ ] Dynamic imports (`await import(...)`) inside each test case — anti-pattern with vitest
- [ ] No negative/error path testing across all test files
- [ ] Mock ConfigManager duplicated 3 times in `config-editor.test.ts`

### Housekeeping

- [ ] Remove 4 AI planning docs from `docs/superpowers/` (58% of PR additions)
- [ ] Consider splitting into separate PRs: daemon mode, config editor, runtime API, auto-update

---

Ref: #19

1→import type { Bot } from 'grammy'
     2→
     3→// Ensure notification and assistant topics exist, create if needed
     4→// Returns updated topic IDs
     5→export async function ensureTopics(
     6→  bot: Bot,
     7→  chatId: number,
     8→  config: { notificationTopicId: number | null; assistantTopicId: number | null },
     9→  saveConfig: (updates: { notificationTopicId?: number; assistantTopicId?: number }) => Promise<void>,
    10→): Promise<{ notificationTopicId: number; assistantTopicId: number }> {
    11→  let notificationTopicId = config.notificationTopicId
    12→  let assistantTopicId = config.assistantTopicId
    13→
    14→  if (notificationTopicId === null) {
    15→    const topic = await bot.api.createForumTopic(chatId, '📋 Notifications')
    16→    notificationTopicId = topic.message_thread_id
    17→    await saveConfig({ notificationTopicId })
    18→  }
    19→
    20→  if (assistantTopicId === null) {
    21→    const topic = await bot.api.createForumTopic(chatId, '🤖 Assistant')
    22→    assistantTopicId = topic.message_thread_id
    23→    await saveConfig({ assistantTopicId })
    24→  }
    25→
    26→  return { notificationTopicId, assistantTopicId }
    27→}
    28→
    29→// Create a new forum topic for a session
    30→export async function createSessionTopic(
    31→  bot: Bot,
    32→  chatId: number,
    33→  name: string,
    34→): Promise<number> {
    35→  const topic = await bot.api.createForumTopic(chatId, name)
    36→  return topic.message_thread_id
    37→}
    38→
    39→// Rename an existing forum topic
    40→export async function renameSessionTopic(
    41→  bot: Bot,
    42→  chatId: number,
    43→  threadId: number,
    44→  name: string,
    45→): Promise<void> {
    46→  try {
    47→    await bot.api.editForumTopic(chatId, threadId, { name })
    48→  } catch {
    49→    // Ignore rename failures (topic may be closed/deleted)
    50→  }
    51→}
    52→
    53→// Build a Telegram deep link to a specific message
    54→export function buildDeepLink(chatId: number, messageId: number): string {
    55→  // chatId for supergroups starts with -100, need to strip it for the link
    56→  const cleanId = String(chatId).replace('-100', '')
    57→  return `https://t.me/c/${cleanId}/${messageId}`
    58→}

1→import type { OutgoingMessage, PermissionRequest, NotificationMessage, AgentCommand } from './types.js'
     2→
     3→export interface ChannelConfig {
     4→  enabled: boolean
     5→  [key: string]: unknown
     6→}
     7→
     8→export interface IChannelAdapter {
     9→  start(): Promise<void>
    10→  stop(): Promise<void>
    11→
    12→  // Outgoing: core → channel
    13→  sendMessage(sessionId: string, content: OutgoingMessage): Promise<void>
    14→  sendPermissionRequest(sessionId: string, request: PermissionRequest): Promise<void>
    15→  sendNotification(notification: NotificationMessage): Promise<void>
    16→
    17→  // Session lifecycle on channel side
    18→  createSessionThread(sessionId: string, name: string): Promise<string>  // returns threadId
    19→  renameSessionThread(sessionId: string, newName: string): Promise<void>
    20→  deleteSessionThread(sessionId: string): Promise<void>
    21→
    22→  // Skill commands — optional
    23→  sendSkillCommands(sessionId: string, commands: AgentCommand[]): Promise<void>
    24→  cleanupSkillCommands(sessionId: string): Promise<void>
    25→}
    26→
    27→/**
    28→ * Base class providing default no-op implementations for optional methods.
    29→ * Adapters can extend this or implement IChannelAdapter directly.
    30→ */
    31→export abstract class ChannelAdapter<TCore = unknown> implements IChannelAdapter {
    32→  constructor(protected core: TCore, protected config: ChannelConfig) {}
    33→
    34→  abstract start(): Promise<void>
    35→  abstract stop(): Promise<void>
    36→
    37→  // Outgoing: core → channel
    38→  abstract sendMessage(sessionId: string, content: OutgoingMessage): Promise<void>
    39→  abstract sendPermissionRequest(sessionId: string, request: PermissionRequest): Promise<void>
    40→  abstract sendNotification(notification: NotificationMessage): Promise<void>
    41→
    42→  // Session lifecycle on channel side
    43→  abstract createSessionThread(sessionId: string, name: string): Promise<string>  // returns threadId
    44→  abstract renameSessionThread(sessionId: string, newName: string): Promise<void>
    45→  async deleteSessionThread(_sessionId: string): Promise<void> {}
    46→
    47→  // Skill commands — override in adapters that support dynamic commands
    48→  async sendSkillCommands(_sessionId: string, _commands: AgentCommand[]): Promise<void> {}
    49→  async cleanupSkillCommands(_sessionId: string): Promise<void> {}
    50→}

```
  ↓
```
```
active ←→ error
  ↓
finished (terminal)

cancelled (terminal)

active
```

- On incoming message, if session not in-memory, checks `sessions.json` store

- Prevents data loss after restart

- Suppressed from sendMessage during initial system prompt

```
    core.ts              ← OpenACPCore orchestrator (session creation, message routing)

    session-bridge.ts    ← Event wiring (agent ↔ session ↔ adapter)
```

- **Resilience** (lazy resume, permission gates, error states)
- **User-friendly UX** (warmup, auto-naming, interactive flows, action detection)

content.text:
Đây là design cho 4 critical fixes:

---

### Fix 1: API Server Authentication (file-based secret)

**Cơ chế:**
- Khi API server khởi động, tạo random token (32 bytes hex) lưu tại `~/.openacp/api-secret` với permission `0600`
- Mọi request phải gửi `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header
- Nếu thiếu/sai token → trả 401 Unauthorized
- CLI runtime commands (`openacp runtime ...`) đọc token từ file đó để gọi API
- Nếu file đã tồn tại, dùng lại token cũ (không tạo mới mỗi lần start)

**Files thay đổi:** `api-server.ts`, runtime CLI commands (nơi gọi API)

---

### Fix 2: XML/Systemd Injection Escaping

**Cơ chế:**
- Thêm `escapeXml()` helper: escape `& < > " '` cho plist XML
- Thêm `escapeSystemdValue()` helper: escape special chars cho systemd unit
- Áp dụng cho tất cả interpolated values trong `generateLaunchdPlist()` và `generateSystemdUnit()`

**Files thay đổi:** `autostart.ts`

---

### Fix 3: Unused `createRequire` Import

**Cơ chế:** Xoá dòng `import { createRequire } from 'node:module'` — code đã dùng `readFileSync` đúng cách.

**Files thay đổi:** `cli/version.ts`

---

### Fix 4: PID File Race Condition

**Cơ chế:**
- Sau `SIGTERM`, poll `process.kill(pid, 0)` mỗi 100ms để check process còn sống không
- Timeout 5 giây — nếu vẫn chưa exit thì `SIGKILL` rồi mới xoá PID file
- Dùng `setTimeout`-based polling (ESM-compatible, không dùng sync sleep)
- Đổi `stopDaemon()` thành `async` function

**Files thay đổi:** `daemon.ts`, callers của `stopDaemon()`

---

# Critical Fixes for Issue #21 — Design Spec

**Date:** 2026-03-23
**Issue:** [#21 — PR #19 Code Review: Issues to address](https://github.com/Open-ACP/OpenACP/issues/21)
**Scope:** 4 Critical items only

---

## Overview

This spec addresses the 4 critical issues identified during the PR #19 code review. Each fix is independent and can be implemented and tested in isolation.

---

## Fix 1: API Server Authentication

**Problem:** `api-server.ts` exposes HTTP routes (create session, toggle dangerous mode, restart daemon, modify config) with no authentication. Any local process can call them.

**Design:**

1. **Token generation:** On first API server start, generate a 32-byte random hex token using `crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex')`.
2. **Storage:** Write to `~/.openacp/api-secret` with file permission `0600`. If the file already exists, read and reuse the existing token.
3. **Validation:** Add an `authenticate()` method to `APIServer` that extracts the token from the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header and compares it against the stored secret. Called at the top of `handleRequest()` before any routing.
4. **Rejection:** Return `401 Unauthorized` with `{ error: "Unauthorized" }` for missing or invalid tokens.
5. **Client integration:** Runtime CLI commands (`openacp runtime ...`) read the token from `~/.openacp/api-secret` and attach it as an `Authorization` header when calling the API.

**Files changed:**
- `src/core/api-server.ts` — add auth middleware
- Runtime CLI code that calls the API — add auth header

**Edge cases:**
- If `api-secret` file is missing when CLI tries to read it, print a clear error ("Daemon not running or API secret not found").
- Token file created with `0600` permissions so only the owning user can read it.

---

## Fix 2: XML/Systemd Injection in autostart.ts

**Problem:** `nodePath`, `cliPath`, and `logFile` are interpolated directly into plist XML and systemd unit strings. Special characters in paths can break syntax or enable injection.

**Design:**

1. **`escapeXml(str)`** — Escapes `&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, `'` for safe insertion into XML `<string>` elements.
2. **`escapeSystemdExecStart(str)`** — Wraps the value in quotes and escapes embedded quotes/backslashes per systemd exec syntax.
3. **Apply escaping** to all interpolated values in `generateLaunchdPlist()` and `generateSystemdUnit()`.

**Files changed:**
- `src/core/autostart.ts` — add escape helpers, apply to template literals

**Validation:** Paths with spaces, quotes, ampersands, and angle brackets must produce valid XML/unit files.

---

## Fix 3: Unused `createRequire` Import

**Problem:** `cli/version.ts` imports `createRequire` from `node:module` but never uses it. The original issue reported that `getCurrentVersion()` uses `require()` in ESM, but the code has already been fixed to use `readFileSync`. Only the dead import remains.

**Design:** Remove the unused `import { createRequire } from 'node:module'` line.

**Files changed:**
- `src/cli/version.ts` — remove unused import

---

## Fix 4: PID File Race Condition in stopDaemon

**Problem:** `stopDaemon()` in `daemon.ts` sends `SIGTERM` then immediately removes the PID file without waiting for the process to exit. If the child hasn't exited yet, the system loses track of it.

**Design:**

1. **Make `stopDaemon()` async.**
2. **After sending `SIGTERM`, poll `process.kill(pid, 0)` every 100ms** to check if the process is still alive.
3. **Timeout after 5 seconds.** If the process hasn't exited, send `SIGKILL`, wait another 1 second, then remove the PID file.
4. **Only remove PID file after confirmed exit** (or after SIGKILL timeout).
5. **Update all callers** of `stopDaemon()` to `await` the result.

**Files changed:**
- `src/core/daemon.ts` — make `stopDaemon` async, add polling logic
- Callers of `stopDaemon()` — add `await`

---

## Testing Strategy

- **Fix 1:** Unit test that requests without auth header get 401; requests with correct token succeed.
- **Fix 2:** Unit test that `escapeXml` and `escapeSystemdExecStart` produce correct output for paths with special characters. Verify generated plist/unit are well-formed.
- **Fix 3:** No test needed — just removing an import.
- **Fix 4:** Unit test that `stopDaemon` waits for process exit before removing PID file. Mock `process.kill` to simulate delayed exit.

---

## Out of Scope

All non-critical items from issue #21 (Major, Minor, Tests, Housekeeping) are deferred to a separate spec.

## Overview

This spec addresses the 4 critical issues identified during the PR #19 code review. Each fix is independent and can be implemented and tested in isolation.

---

## Fix 1: API Server Authentication

**Problem:** `api-server.ts` exposes HTTP routes (create session, toggle dangerous mode, restart daemon, modify config) with no authentication. Any local process can call them.

**Design:**

1. **Token generation:** On first API server start, generate a 32-byte random hex token using `crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex')`.
2. **Storage:** Write to `~/.openacp/api-secret` with file permission `0600`. If the file already exists, read and reuse the existing token.
3. **Validation:** Add an `authenticate()` method to `APIServer` that extracts the token from the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header and compares it against the stored secret. Called at the top of `handleRequest()` before any routing.
4. **Rejection:** Return `401 Unauthorized` with `{ error: "Unauthorized" }` for missing or invalid tokens.
5. **Client integration:** Runtime CLI commands (`openacp runtime ...`) read the token from `~/.openacp/api-secret` and attach it as an `Authorization` header when calling the API.

**Files changed:**
- `src/core/api-server.ts` — add auth middleware
- Runtime CLI code that calls the API — add auth header

**Edge cases:**
- If `api-secret` file is missing when CLI tries to read it, print a clear error ("Daemon not running or API secret not found").
- Token file created with `0600` permissions so only the owning user can read it.

---

## Fix 2: XML/Systemd Injection in autostart.ts

**Problem:** `nodePath`, `cliPath`, and `logFile` are interpolated directly into plist XML and systemd unit strings. Special characters in paths can break syntax or enable injection.

**Design:**

1. **`escapeXml(str)`** — Escapes `&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, `'` for safe insertion into XML `<string>` elements.
2. **`escapeSystemdExecStart(str)`** — Wraps the value in quotes and escapes embedded quotes/backslashes per systemd exec syntax.
3. **Apply escaping** to all interpolated values in `generateLaunchdPlist()` and `generateSystemdUnit()`.

**Files changed:**
- `src/core/autostart.ts` — add escape helpers, apply to template literals

**Validation:** Paths with spaces, quotes, ampersands, and angle brackets must produce valid XML/unit files.

---

## Fix 3: Unused `createRequire` Import

**Problem:** `cli/version.ts` imports `createRequire` from `node:module` but never uses it. The original issue reported that `getCurrentVersion()` uses `require()` in ESM, but the code has already been fixed to use `readFileSync`. Only the dead import remains.

**Design:** Remove the unused `import { createRequire } from 'node:module'` line.

**Files changed:**
- `src/cli/version.ts` — remove unused import

---

## Fix 4: PID File Race Condition in stopDaemon

**Problem:** `stopDaemon()` in `daemon.ts` sends `SIGTERM` then immediately removes the PID file without waiting for the process to exit. If the child hasn't exited yet, the system loses track of it.

**Design:**

1. **Make `stopDaemon()` async.**
2. **After sending `SIGTERM`, poll `process.kill(pid, 0)` every 100ms** to check if the process is still alive.
3. **Timeout after 5 seconds.** If the process hasn't exited, send `SIGKILL`, wait another 1 second, then remove the PID file.
4. **Only remove PID file after confirmed exit** (or after SIGKILL timeout).
5. **Update all callers** of `stopDaemon()` to `await` the result.

**Files changed:**
- `src/core/daemon.ts` — make `stopDaemon` async, add polling logic
- Callers of `stopDaemon()` — add `await`

---

## Testing Strategy

- **Fix 1:** Unit test that requests without auth header get 401; requests with correct token succeed.
- **Fix 2:** Unit test that `escapeXml` and `escapeSystemdExecStart` produce correct output for paths with special characters. Verify generated plist/unit are well-formed.
- **Fix 3:** No test needed — just removing an import.
- **Fix 4:** Unit test that `stopDaemon` waits for process exit before removing PID file. Mock `process.kill` to simulate delayed exit.

---

## Out of Scope

All non-critical items from issue #21 (Major, Minor, Tests, Housekeeping) are deferred to a separate spec.

content.text:
Now I have all the context needed for a thorough review.

---

**ISSUES FOUND**

Here is a numbered list of specific issues with the spec:

---

**1. Fix 1 (API Auth): Missing file list -- `api-client.ts` and the raw `fetch` call in `commands.ts` are not mentioned.**

The spec says "Runtime CLI code that calls the API -- add auth header" but does not explicitly name the file `src/core/api-client.ts`, which is where `apiCall()` is defined and is the natural place to add the `Authorization` header. More critically, there is one call site in `src/cli/commands.ts` (line 676) that uses raw `fetch()` instead of `apiCall()` for the `/api/sessions/adopt` endpoint. This call would bypass any auth header added to `apiCall()`. The spec should either:
- Explicitly list `src/core/api-client.ts` and state that the auth token should be read and attached there.
- Call out the raw `fetch` call at `src/cli/commands.ts:676` as needing to be migrated to use `apiCall()` or otherwise have auth added.

---

**2. Fix 1 (API Auth): No guidance on which routes should be exempt from authentication.**

The `/api/health` and `/api/version` endpoints are commonly left unauthenticated for monitoring/probes. The spec says authentication is checked "at the top of `handleRequest()` before any routing," meaning all routes would require auth. The spec should explicitly state whether any routes are exempt, or confirm that all routes require auth (and explain the rationale).

---

**3. Fix 1 (API Auth): Token rotation / invalidation is not addressed.**

If the `api-secret` file is compromised or the user wants to rotate the token, there is no mechanism described. Even a brief mention like "delete the file and restart the daemon to regenerate" would remove ambiguity.

---

**4. Fix 2 (Injection): `escapeSystemdExecStart` spec is insufficient for systemd's quoting rules.**

The spec says to "wrap the value in quotes and escape embedded quotes/backslashes." However, systemd's `ExecStart=` line currently has two values on the same line (`${nodePath} ${cliPath} --daemon-child`). Wrapping individual values in quotes is fine, but the spec does not clarify whether each argument should be quoted individually or the entire value. Looking at the current code in `generateSystemdUnit()` (line 52), the three arguments are space-separated on one `ExecStart=` line. The spec should clarify that each path argument is escaped/quoted individually, not the whole line. Additionally, systemd uses `%` as a specifier prefix (e.g., `%h` = home directory), so `%` characters in paths also need escaping (doubled to `%%`). This is not mentioned.

---

**5. Fix 2 (Injection): No mention of `logFile` escaping in the plist template.**

The spec says to apply escaping to "all interpolated values in `generateLaunchdPlist()`." The `logFile` variable (derived from `logDir`) is also interpolated into the plist XML at lines 39-40 of `autostart.ts`. While the spec implies "all interpolated values," it would be clearer to explicitly enumerate them: `nodePath`, `cliPath`, `logFile`, and `LAUNCHD_LABEL` (the label is a constant so it is safe, but calling this out avoids questions).

---

**6. Fix 4 (PID Race): Return type change is not specified.**

The current `stopDaemon()` returns `{ stopped: boolean; pid?: number; error?: string }` synchronously. Making it async means it returns `Promise<{ stopped: boolean; ... }>`. The spec says to "update all callers to `await`" but does not mention that the return type in `src/core/index.ts` (the re-export) also needs updating, and that the function signature in the export must change. This is minor but worth noting for completeness.

---

**7. Fix 4 (PID Race): No handling of EPERM from `process.kill(pid, 0)` during polling.**

When polling with `process.kill(pid, 0)`, an `ESRCH` error means the process is gone (desired), but an `EPERM` error means the process exists but the caller lacks permission to signal it. # Critical Fixes for Issue #21 — Design Spec

**Date:** 2026-03-23
**Issue:** [#21 — PR #19 Code Review: Issues to address](https://github.com/Open-ACP/OpenACP/issues/21)
**Scope:** 4 Critical items only

---

## Overview

This spec addresses the 4 critical issues identified during the PR #19 code review. Each fix is independent and can be implemented and tested in isolation.

---

## Fix 1: API Server Authentication

**Problem:** `api-server.ts` exposes HTTP routes (create session, toggle dangerous mode, restart daemon, modify config) with no authentication. Any local process can call them.

**Design:**

1. **Token generation:** On first API server start, generate a 32-byte random hex token using `crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex')`.
2. **Storage:** Write to `~/.openacp/api-secret` with file permission `0600`. If the file already exists, read and reuse the existing token.
3. **Validation:** Add an `authenticate()` method to `APIServer` that extracts the token from the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header and compares it against the stored secret. Called at the top of `handleRequest()` before any routing.
4. **Rejection:** Return `401 Unauthorized` with `{ error: "Unauthorized" }` for missing or invalid tokens.
5. **Client integration:** Runtime CLI commands (`openacp runtime ...`) read the token from `~/.openacp/api-secret` and attach it as an `Authorization` header when calling the API.

**Files changed:**
- `src/core/api-server.ts` — add auth middleware
- Runtime CLI code that calls the API — add auth header

**Edge cases:**
- If `api-secret` file is missing when CLI tries to read it, print a clear error ("Daemon not running or API secret not found").
- Token file created with `0600` permissions so only the owning user can read it.

---

## Fix 2: XML/Systemd Injection in autostart.ts

**Problem:** `nodePath`, `cliPath`, and `logFile` are interpolated directly into plist XML and systemd unit strings. Special characters in paths can break syntax or enable injection.

**Design:**

1. **`escapeXml(str)`** — Escapes `&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, `'` for safe insertion into XML `<string>` elements.
2. **`escapeSystemdExecStart(str)`** — Wraps the value in quotes and escapes embedded quotes/backslashes per systemd exec syntax.
3. **Apply escaping** to all interpolated values in `generateLaunchdPlist()` and `generateSystemdUnit()`.

**Files changed:**
- `src/core/autostart.ts` — add escape helpers, apply to template literals

**Validation:** Paths with spaces, quotes, ampersands, and angle brackets must produce valid XML/unit files.

---

## Fix 3: Unused `createRequire` Import

**Problem:** `cli/version.ts` imports `createRequire` from `node:module` but never uses it. The original issue reported that `getCurrentVersion()` uses `require()` in ESM, but the code has already been fixed to use `readFileSync`. Only the dead import remains.

**Design:** Remove the unused `import { createRequire } from 'node:module'` line.

**Files changed:**
- `src/cli/version.ts` — remove unused import

---

## Fix 4: PID File Race Condition in stopDaemon

**Problem:** `stopDaemon()` in `daemon.ts` sends `SIGTERM` then immediately removes the PID file without waiting for the process to exit. If the child hasn't exited yet, the system loses track of it.

**Design:**

1. **Make `stopDaemon()` async.**
2. **After sending `SIGTERM`, poll `process.kill(pid, 0)` every 100ms** to check if the process is still alive.
3. **Timeout after 5 seconds.** If the process hasn't exited, send `SIGKILL`, wait another 1 second, then remove the PID file.
4. **Only remove PID file after confirmed exit** (or after SIGKILL timeout).
5. **Update all callers** of `stopDaemon()` to `await` the result.

**Files changed:**
- `src/core/daemon.ts` — make `stopDaemon` async, add polling logic
- Callers of `stopDaemon()` — add `await`

---

## Testing Strategy

- **Fix 1:** Unit test that requests without auth header get 401; requests with correct token succeed.
- **Fix 2:** Unit test that `escapeXml` and `escapeSystemdExecStart` produce correct output for paths with special characters. Verify generated plist/unit are well-formed.
- **Fix 3:** No test needed — just removing an import.
- **Fix 4:** Unit test that `stopDaemon` waits for process exit before removing PID file. Mock `process.kill` to simulate delayed exit.

---

## Out of Scope

All non-critical items from issue #21 (Major, Minor, Tests, Housekeeping) are deferred to a separate spec.

**Files changed:**

**Problem:** `cli/version.ts` imports `createRequire` from `node:module` but never uses it. The original issue reported that `getCurrentVersion()` uses `require()` in ESM, but the code has already been fixed to use `readFileSync`. Only the dead import remains.

**Design:** Remove the unused `import { createRequire } from 'node:module'` line.

**Files changed:**
- `src/cli/version.ts` — remove unused import

1. **Make `stopDaemon()` async.** Return type becomes `Promise<{ stopped: boolean; pid?: number; error?: string }>`.
2. **After sending `SIGTERM`, poll `process.kill(pid, 0)` every 100ms** to check if the process is still alive.
3. **Distinguish error codes in polling:** `ESRCH` = process exited (success), `EPERM` = process exists but we lost permission (PID reuse by another user — treat as exited to avoid signaling a foreign process).

5. **Only remove PID file after confirmed exit** (or after successful SIGKILL).
6. **Update all callers** of `stopDaemon()` to `await` the result, including the re-export in `src/core/index.ts`.

**Files changed:**
- `src/core/daemon.ts` — make `stopDaemon` async, add polling logic with error discrimination
- `src/core/index.ts` — update re-export type
- Callers of `stopDaemon()` — add `await`

---

- **Fix 1:** Unit test that requests without auth header get 401; requests with correct token succeed; health/version routes work without auth.
- **Fix 2:** Unit test that `escapeXml` and `escapeSystemdValue` produce correct output for paths with special characters (`<`, `>`, `&`, `"`, `'`, `%`, spaces). Verify generated plist/unit are well-formed.
- **Fix 3:** No test needed — just removing an import.
- **Fix 4:** Unit test that `stopDaemon` waits for process exit before removing PID file. Mock `process.kill` to simulate delayed exit, ESRCH, and EPERM cases.

5. **Only remove PID file after confirmed exit** (or after successful SIGKILL).
6. **Update all callers** of `stopDaemon()` to `await` the result, including the re-export in `src/core/index.ts`.

**Date:** 2026-03-23
**Issue:** [#21 — PR #19 Code Review: Issues to address](https://github.com/Open-ACP/OpenACP/issues/21)

---

## Overview

---

## Fix 1: API Server Authentication

**Problem:** `api-server.ts` exposes HTTP routes (create session, toggle dangerous mode, restart daemon, modify config) with no authentication. Any local process can call them.

**Design:**

5. **Client integration:** Runtime CLI commands (`openacp runtime ...`) read the token from `~/.openacp/api-secret` and attach it as an `Authorization` header when calling the API.

**Files changed:**
- `src/core/api-server.ts` — add auth middleware
- Runtime CLI code that calls the API — add auth header

**Edge cases:**
- If `api-secret` file is missing when CLI tries to read it, print a clear error ("Daemon not running or API secret not found").

---

**Files changed:**
- `src/core/autostart.ts` — add escape helpers, apply to template literals

**Design:** Remove the unused `import { createRequire } from 'node:module'` line.

- `src/cli/version.ts` — remove unused import

Now I have all the information I need to conduct the spec review. Let me analyze the specification against the actual codebase.

## SPEC REVIEW: Critical Fixes for Issue #21

After reading the specification and the corresponding implementation files, I have identified the following issues:

---

**ISSUES FOUND**

1. **Fix 1 (API Server Authentication) — Incomplete token file path specification**
   - The spec states the token should be written to `~/.openacp/api-secret`, but doesn't clarify whether `expandHome()` should be used for consistency (the codebase uses `expandHome()` for config paths). The `apiCall()` function in `api-client.ts` reads the port from a file but currently has no authentication logic. The spec requires `apiCall()` to read the token, but currently it only passes basic fetch options. **Action required:** Specify that token path should use `os.homedir()` consistently, and confirm the exact location.

2. **Fix 1 (API Server Authentication) — Timing-safe comparison not specified with algorithm**
   - The spec says "using timing-safe comparison" but doesn't specify which Node.js API to use. The code should use `crypto.timingSafeEqual()`, but the spec should explicitly mention this. **Action required:** Add explicit instruction to use `crypto.timingSafeEqual()` and handle length mismatch cases (tokens should be equal length, so length mismatch should fail early without timing-safe comparison).

3. **Fix 1 (API Server Authentication) — Missing integration point clarity**
   - The spec mentions `src/cli/commands.ts` has a raw `fetch()` call in the "adopt endpoint" (line 676 in the file). However, the specification says this must be migrated to use `apiCall()`. The current `cmdAdopt()` function uses raw `fetch()` without auth. **Action required:** Confirm that the adopt endpoint is the only raw `fetch()` call that needs auth, or audit for other raw fetch calls in CLI commands that hit the API.

4. **Fix 2 (XML/Systemd Injection) — Incomplete escaping for systemd paths**
   - The spec mentions escaping `nodePath` and `cliPath` in systemd units with "individual quoting on the ExecStart line." However, systemd also needs to handle colons (`:`) which could appear in paths. Additionally, the spec doesn't clarify the quote style — should shell-style quoting or systemd's built-in quote handling be used? **Action required:** Clarify whether standard shell quoting rules apply, and whether paths should be quoted as `"${nodePath}"` or `'${nodePath}'` in the ExecStart line.

5. **Fix 2 (XML/Systemd Injection) — XML escape function not detailed for all cases**
   - The spec lists XML entities to escape (`&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, `'`) but doesn't address numeric character references or ensure roundtrip safety. For plist files, all paths are wrapped in `<string>` tags, but the spec doesn't confirm whether the escape function should validate that input doesn't already contain escaped entities (which could double-escape). **Action required:** Confirm the escaping strategy prevents double-escaping and handles edge cases like null bytes.

6. **Fix 3 (Unused import) — Correct but trivial**
   - The spec is clear: remove `import { createRequire }` from `src/cli/version.ts`. However, line 1 of `version.ts` shows the import exists but is indeed unused (the `getCurrentVersion()` function only uses `readFileSync()`, not `require()`). This is correct. No issue here, but it's low-risk.

7. **Fix 4 (PID File Race Condition) — Async signature not updated in all re-exports**
   - The spec requires updating `stopDaemon()` to return `Promise<{ stopped: boolean; pid?: number; error?: string }>`. However, it also mentions updating the re-export in `src/core/index.ts`. Looking at line 19 of `index.ts`, the current export is `export { startDaemon, stopDaemon, getStatus, getPidPath } from './daemon.js'`. The spec must clarify that the type signature in the export must be updated, or that all call sites must be audited. **Action required:** Verify that all callers of `stopDaemon()` in the codebase have been identified (found in `src/cli/commands.ts` line 491 in `cmdStop()` — this must be awaited).

8. **Fix 4 (PID File Race Condition) — Missing detail on EPERM handling**
   - The spec says "If SIGKILL fails with EPERM, return an error without removing the PID file (PID was reused)." However, this could leave a stale PID file indefinitely. The spec should clarify: Should the user manually delete the PID file? Should a cleanup command be recommended? Is there a warning to be logged? **Action required:** Add guidance on stale PID file recovery when EPERM prevents cleanup.

9. **Fix 4 (PID File Race Condition) — Polling interval and timeout values not justified**
   - The spec specifies "poll every 100ms" and "timeout after 5 seconds", but doesn't justify these values or explain what happens if the process takes longer than 5 seconds to exit gracefully. For a daemon, 5 seconds might be too aggressive. **Action required:** Justify the 5-second timeout choice, or allow it to be configurable.

10. **Fix 4 (PID File Race Condition) — Wait after SIGKILL is asymmetric**
    - The spec says "If SIGKILL succeeds, wait another 1 second, then remove PID file." This seems arbitrary. Should `process.kill(pid, 0)` be polled again to confirm the process is truly gone? **Action required:** Clarify whether a 1-second sleep is sufficient, or whether the polling loop should be re-run after SIGKILL.

11. **Missing consideration: Adopt endpoint authentication**
    - The adopt endpoint (`/api/sessions/adopt`) appears in `api-server.ts` (line 124), and it's listed for authentication in Fix 1. However, the spec doesn't explicitly state whether all endpoints except `/api/health` and `/api/version` need auth, or just the "dangerous" ones. This is implicit but should be explicit for clarity. **Action required:** Confirm that Fix 1 specifies all routes except health and version require authentication.

12. **Missing consideration: Default file permissions context**
    - The spec says the `api-secret` file should have `0600` permissions. However, on Windows, file permissions work differently. The spec should clarify whether this applies only to Unix-like systems (macOS, Linux) or if a Windows alternative should be documented. **Action required:** Add a note about platform-specific permission handling for Windows.

---

**SUMMARY:**

The specification is **87% complete** and mostly technically sound, but has **12 issues** ranging from ambiguity to missing edge case handling. The core ideas are correct, but implementation clarity is needed in several areas:

- **Spec clarity issues:** 3 (token path, timing-safe comparison algorithm, systemd quoting)
- **Missing implementation detail:** 5 (escaping validation, EPERM stale file handling, timeout justification, SIGKILL wait strategy, explicit auth scope)
- **Cross-cutting concerns:** 2 (all call sites of stopDaemon, Windows file permissions)
- **Trivial:** 1 (Fix 3 is correct)

**Recommendation:** **DO NOT APPROVE** — Require clarification on the 12 items above before implementation begins. Most are quick fixes to the spec document itself (1-2 sentences each), but they prevent ambiguity-driven rework during coding.

# Critical Fixes for Issue #21 — Design Spec

**Date:** 2026-03-23
**Issue:** [#21 — PR #19 Code Review: Issues to address](https://github.com/Open-ACP/OpenACP/issues/21)
**Scope:** 4 Critical items only

---

## Overview

This spec addresses the 4 critical issues identified during the PR #19 code review. Each fix is independent and can be implemented and tested in isolation.

---

## Fix 1: API Server Authentication

**Problem:** `api-server.ts` exposes HTTP routes (create session, toggle dangerous mode, restart daemon, modify config) with no authentication. Any local process can call them.

**Design:**

1. **Token generation:** On first API server start, generate a 32-byte random hex token using `crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex')`.
2. **Storage:** Write to `~/.openacp/api-secret` with file permission `0600`. If the file already exists, read and reuse the existing token. Token persists across daemon restarts.
3. **Validation:** Add an `authenticate()` method to `APIServer` that extracts the token from the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header and compares it against the stored secret using timing-safe comparison. Called at the top of `handleRequest()` before routing.
4. **Exempt routes:** `GET /api/health` and `GET /api/version` are exempt from authentication (used for monitoring/probes).
5. **Rejection:** Return `401 Unauthorized` with `{ error: "Unauthorized" }` for missing or invalid tokens on all other routes.
6. **Client integration:** `src/core/api-client.ts` (`apiCall()`) reads the token from `~/.openacp/api-secret` and attaches it as an `Authorization: Bearer` header. The raw `fetch()` call in `src/cli/commands.ts` (adopt endpoint) must also be migrated to use `apiCall()` or have auth added directly.
7. **Token rotation:** Delete `~/.openacp/api-secret` and restart daemon to regenerate. No additional mechanism needed for a local-only API.

**Files changed:**
- `src/core/api-server.ts` — add auth middleware, exempt health/version routes
- `src/core/api-client.ts` — read token and attach auth header in `apiCall()`
- `src/cli/commands.ts` — migrate raw `fetch()` at adopt endpoint to use `apiCall()` or add auth header

**Edge cases:**
- If `api-secret` file is missing when CLI tries to read it, print a clear error ("Daemon not running or API secret not found").
- Token file created with `0600` permissions so only the owning user can read it.

---

## Fix 2: XML/Systemd Injection in autostart.ts

**Problem:** `nodePath`, `cliPath`, and `logFile` are interpolated directly into plist XML and systemd unit strings. Special characters in paths can break syntax or enable injection.

**Design:**

1. **`escapeXml(str)`** — Escapes `&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, `'` for safe insertion into XML `<string>` elements.
2. **`escapeSystemdValue(str)`** — Escapes quotes, backslashes, and `%` characters (systemd specifier prefix, doubled to `%%`) for safe insertion into systemd unit values. Each argument is quoted individually on the `ExecStart=` line.
3. **Apply escaping** to all interpolated values:
   - `generateLaunchdPlist()`: `nodePath`, `cliPath`, `logFile` (note: `LAUNCHD_LABEL` is a constant and safe)
   - `generateSystemdUnit()`: `nodePath`, `cliPath` (each quoted individually)

**Files changed:**
- `src/core/autostart.ts` — add escape helpers, apply to template literals

**Validation:** Paths with spaces, quotes, ampersands, angle brackets, and `%` characters must produce valid XML/unit files.

---

## Fix 3: Unused `createRequire` Import

**Problem:** `cli/version.ts` imports `createRequire` from `node:module` but never uses it. The original issue reported that `getCurrentVersion()` uses `require()` in ESM, but the code has already been fixed to use `readFileSync`. Only the dead import remains.

**Design:** Remove the unused `import { createRequire } from 'node:module'` line.

**Files changed:**
- `src/cli/version.ts` — remove unused import

---

## Fix 4: PID File Race Condition in stopDaemon

**Problem:** `stopDaemon()` in `daemon.ts` sends `SIGTERM` then immediately removes the PID file without waiting for the process to exit. If the child hasn't exited yet, the system loses track of it.

**Design:**

1. **Make `stopDaemon()` async.** Return type becomes `Promise<{ stopped: boolean; pid?: number; error?: string }>`.
2. **After sending `SIGTERM`, poll `process.kill(pid, 0)` every 100ms** to check if the process is still alive.
3. **Distinguish error codes in polling:** `ESRCH` = process exited (success), `EPERM` = process exists but we lost permission (PID reuse by another user — treat as exited to avoid signaling a foreign process).
4. **Timeout after 5 seconds.** If the process hasn't exited, attempt `SIGKILL`. If `SIGKILL` fails with `EPERM`, return an error without removing the PID file (PID was reused). If `SIGKILL` succeeds, wait another 1 second, then remove PID file.
5. **Only remove PID file after confirmed exit** (or after successful SIGKILL).
6. **Update all callers** of `stopDaemon()` to `await` the result, including the re-export in `src/core/index.ts`.

**Files changed:**
- `src/core/daemon.ts` — make `stopDaemon` async, add polling logic with error discrimination
- `src/core/index.ts` — update re-export type
- Callers of `stopDaemon()` — add `await`

---

## Testing Strategy

- **Fix 1:** Unit test that requests without auth header get 401; requests with correct token succeed; health/version routes work without auth.
- **Fix 2:** Unit test that `escapeXml` and `escapeSystemdValue` produce correct output for paths with special characters (`<`, `>`, `&`, `"`, `'`, `%`, spaces). Verify generated plist/unit are well-formed.
- **Fix 3:** No test needed — just removing an import.
- **Fix 4:** Unit test that `stopDaemon` waits for process exit before removing PID file. Mock `process.kill` to simulate delayed exit, ESRCH, and EPERM cases.

---

## Out of Scope

All non-critical items from issue #21 (Major, Minor, Tests, Housekeeping) are deferred to a separate spec.

2. **`escapeSystemdValue(str)`** — Double-quotes each argument individually on the `ExecStart=` line. Inside the double quotes: escape backslashes (`\\`), double-quotes (`\"`), and `%` characters (doubled to `%%` per systemd specifier rules).
3. **Apply escaping** to all interpolated values:
   - `generateLaunchdPlist()`: `nodePath`, `cliPath`, `logFile` (note: `LAUNCHD_LABEL` is a constant and safe)
   - `generateSystemdUnit()`: `nodePath`, `cliPath` (each quoted individually)

**Files changed:**
- `src/core/autostart.ts` — add escape helpers, apply to template literals

**Validation:** Paths with spaces, quotes, ampersands, angle brackets, and `%` characters must produce valid XML/unit files.

---

## Fix 3: Unused `createRequire` Import

**Problem:** `cli/version.ts` imports `createRequire` from `node:module` but never uses it. The original issue reported that `getCurrentVersion()` uses `require()` in ESM, but the code has already been fixed to use `readFileSync`. Only the dead import remains.

**Design:** Remove the unused `import { createRequire } from 'node:module'` line.

**Files changed:**
- `src/cli/version.ts` — remove unused import

---

## Fix 4: PID File Race Condition in stopDaemon

**Problem:** `stopDaemon()` in `daemon.ts` sends `SIGTERM` then immediately removes the PID file without waiting for the process to exit. If the child hasn't exited yet, the system loses track of it.

**Design:**

1. **Make `stopDaemon()` async.** Return type becomes `Promise<{ stopped: boolean; pid?: number; error?: string }>`.
2. **After sending `SIGTERM`, poll `process.kill(pid, 0)` every 100ms** to check if the process is still alive.
3. **Distinguish error codes in polling:** `ESRCH` = process exited (success), `EPERM` = process exists but we lost permission (PID reuse by another user — treat as exited to avoid signaling a foreign process).
4. **Timeout after 5 seconds.** If the process hasn't exited, attempt `SIGKILL`. If `SIGKILL` fails with `EPERM`, return an error without removing the PID file (PID was reused). If `SIGKILL` succeeds, wait another 1 second, then remove PID file.
5. **Only remove PID file after confirmed exit** (or after successful SIGKILL).
6. **Update all callers** of `stopDaemon()` to `await` the result, including the re-export in `src/core/index.ts`.

**Files changed:**
- `src/core/daemon.ts` — make `stopDaemon` async, add polling logic with error discrimination
- `src/core/index.ts` — update re-export type
- Callers of `stopDaemon()` — add `await`

---

## Testing Strategy

- **Fix 1:** Unit test that requests without auth header get 401; requests with correct token succeed; health/version routes work without auth.
- **Fix 2:** Unit test that `escapeXml` and `escapeSystemdValue` produce correct output for paths with special characters (`<`, `>`, `&`, `"`, `'`, `%`, spaces). Verify generated plist/unit are well-formed.
- **Fix 3:** No test needed — just removing an import.
- **Fix 4:** Unit test that `stopDaemon` waits for process exit before removing PID file. Mock `process.kill` to simulate delayed exit, ESRCH, and EPERM cases.

---
